endpoints.description: Answers as long as the process is up. It touches nothing else on purpose: a liveness probe that checks the database restarts a healthy API every time the database hiccups.

Whether this instance can actually serve traffic: MongoDB reachable, and the deployment a REPLICA SET rather than a standalone mongod. Transactions do not exist on standalone, and without them the checkout stock reservation cannot be atomic — so a standalone deployment is not ready even though it answers.

endpoints.summary: Resolve a serviceable PIN code to its approximate centre
endpoints.description: The non-map way to get a delivery point. `CreateAddressDto` requires lat/lng, and the web app normally collects them from a map pin — which is unavailable wherever Google Maps is not billed. Reads the same static table as `?pincode=` on the two browse routes; never a paid geocoding call. An unserviceable PIN is a 400 carrying `PINCODE_NOT_SERVICEABLE` and the list that does work.

endpoints.summary: Market-wide search and aisle browsing, across every store
endpoints.description: The store-scoped listing above is `GET /stores/:id/products`; this is its platform-wide sibling — every APPROVED, OPEN vendor's products, filtered by `q` (the `searchText` text index, never a regex scan) and/or `aisleKey`. Each row carries `store:{id,slug,storeName,distanceKm}`; `distanceKm` is null unless `lat`/`lng` or a serviceable `pincode` were supplied. Neither FILTERS here — they only measure. There is no `radius`; that belongs to `GET /stores`, where it actually narrows the list.

endpoints.summary: Razorpay payment webhook — the source of truth (§8.3)
endpoints.description: HMAC-verified over the raw body. Always answers 200 for a validly-signed event (even one this platform ignores), because a non-2xx makes Razorpay retry forever; answers 401 only when the signature itself is missing or wrong.

endpoints.description: Every line is compared to the live product and inventory. Per-line `flags` report `price_changed`, `out_of_stock`, `reduced_qty` and `unavailable`. Nothing is silently corrected: a stale cart is the single biggest cause of a failed checkout, and the customer has to be the one who decides what to do about it.

endpoints.summary: The rider's profile and today's figures
endpoints.description: Profile, current location and today's deliveries, earnings (integer paise) and online minutes. Online minutes are measured from the live socket rather than the `isOnline` flag — a rider whose app is closed is not online however the flag was left.
Offers that are still `offered` and not yet past their 45-second `expiresAt`, with pickup, drop, distance, payout and a millisecond countdown so the app does not depend on the handset clock.

endpoints.summary: One offer in full — the confirm screen
endpoints.description: Everything the rider must see BEFORE the money moves: the item list, pickup and drop, the payout, their current balance, and the bounds the pick fee will be drawn from. The exact fee is drawn at accept time, so the range is the only statement that is true when it is made — and showing nothing would mean the rider discovers the charge after it has been taken.

endpoints.summary: Take the job — and pay the pick fee
endpoints.description: Moves the order READY_FOR_PICKUP → ASSIGNED, holds the rider and charges a RANDOM pick fee in [RIDER_PICK_FEE_MIN_PAISE, RIDER_PICK_FEE_MAX_PAISE], all in ONE transaction. Any competing offer on the same order is cancelled. Returns the active order plus `pickFeePaise` and the resulting `walletBalancePaise`, so the app can show the charge the instant it happens.

The order goes to the next nearest rider immediately, with `attemptNo` incremented. After three attempts it escalates to the vendor and the admin console instead of looping. Returns the rider's remaining live offers.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Why the rider declined. Feeds the dispatch quality view.

endpoints.summary: OUT_FOR_DELIVERY → DELIVERED, with the customer's OTP
endpoints.description: The code is compared against a stored hash in constant time. A wrong code is 400 with `attemptsRemaining`; the fifth wrong code LOCKS the delivery (423) and only an admin can complete it. The code is never logged or echoed back.

fields.name: otp
fields.description: The proof-of-delivery OTP read out by the customer. Compared against a HASH in constant time; never logged, never echoed back.

fields.name: photoUrl
fields.description: Optional handover photo, already uploaded to storage.

endpoints.description: A reason is mandatory. The rider is released for other work; the order becomes a support case and can be reassigned.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Mandatory. A failed delivery becomes a support case and somebody has to be able to read what happened.

This is the initial paint; `delivery.location_updated` on the order room moves the marker afterwards, so the app never polls this in a loop.

endpoints.summary: The job in hand, in full
endpoints.description: Pickup and drop with coordinates, the customer contact for the door, the items, the cash to collect (integer paise) and the OTP attempt state. `null` when the rider has no active order.

endpoints.summary: Verification status, masked numbers and documents
endpoints.description: Numbers are MASKED (`XXXX XXXX 1234`). `slaDueAt` and `slaRemainingMs` drive the countdown while the submission is pending; `slaHours` is the promise itself, from `RIDER_KYC_SLA_HOURS`. `canResubmit` is false once VERIFIED.

endpoints.summary: Submit Aadhaar, PAN and driving licence
endpoints.description: Sets status SUBMITTED and stamps `kycSlaDueAt = now + RIDER_KYC_SLA_HOURS`. Formats are validated at the edge — a typo must not consume a human's 24-hour SLA. A rider may resubmit while NOT_STARTED, SUBMITTED or REJECTED; a VERIFIED record is 409, because silently replacing an identity a human approved would make the approval meaningless.

fields.name: aadhaarNumber
fields.description: 12 digits. Spaces are ignored. Stored, never logged.

fields.name: panNumber
fields.description: AAAAA9999A.

fields.name: drivingLicenceNumber
fields.description: 8-20 letters and digits. State formats vary.

endpoints.summary: Presigned PUT for one KYC document
endpoints.description: The file NEVER passes through this API. `contentType` is allowlisted and `sizeBytes` is SIGNED into the URL as `content-length`, so the 5 MB cap is enforced by the bucket rather than suggested to the client. Returns 503 while object storage is unconfigured — which it is on this deployment; the number-based submission above keeps working. PUT the bytes, then POST the returned `publicUrl` back to `/document/attach`.

fields.name: contentType
fields.description: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/avif or application/pdf.

fields.name: sizeBytes

endpoints.summary: Record an upload that has landed
endpoints.description: The URL is checked against the key prefix a presign for THIS rider and THIS document kind would produce, so a rider cannot attach an arbitrary link or another rider's object. One document per kind — a second upload replaces the first.

fields.name: url
fields.description: The `publicUrl` returned by the presign call.

endpoints.summary: Balance, lifetime totals and the low-balance threshold
endpoints.description: Every money field is INTEGER PAISE. `lowBalance` is computed on the server against `RIDER_LOW_BALANCE_WARN_PAISE` — the client is never asked to hold a second copy of a server-side threshold. `pickFeeMinPaise`/`pickFeeMaxPaise` are the bounds the per-order fee is drawn from, so the app can state the cost honestly before the rider commits. The wallet is created at zero on first read.

endpoints.summary: Open a gateway order to add money
endpoints.description: Returns `{ topupId, amountPaise, gatewayOrder }`. Returns 503 `PAYMENT_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED` while Razorpay has no keys — which is the case on this deployment — and writes NOTHING in that case, so there is no orphan attempt and no fabricated success. An administrator can credit the wallet in the meantime.

fields.name: amountPaise
fields.description: INTEGER PAISE. 1000 is ₹10. Never a float, never rupees.

endpoints.summary: Confirm a top-up from the gateway callback
